management.text: [immediate] Ruptured AAA: two large-bore IV cannulae, cross-match 6 units RBC, permissive hypotension (systolic 70–80 mmHg) until in theatre.
[conservative] Small AAA (3.0–5.4 cm): surveillance ultrasound 3-yearly (3–4.4 cm) or annually (4.5–5.4 cm).
[conservative] Cardiovascular risk reduction: statin, antiplatelet, smoking cessation, blood pressure control.
[surgical] Elective repair for AAA ≥5.5 cm (men) / ≥5.0 cm (women), or symptomatic/rapidly expanding: EVAR preferred where anatomy permits.
[surgical] Open surgical repair (midline laparotomy, aortic graft) for anatomy unsuitable for EVAR or EVAR failure.
[followup] Post-EVAR: CT at 1 month, 12 months, then annually for endoleak surveillance.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA): defined as aortic diameter >3 cm; risk of rupture rises sharply above 5.5 cm (men) and 5.0 cm (women).
Rupture presents as triad of hypotension, back/abdominal pain, and pulsatile abdominal mass — mortality without surgery >90%.
Symptomatic or rapidly expanding AAA (>1 cm/year or >0.5 cm/6 months) warrants urgent repair regardless of size.
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.
• Document bilateral BP — coarctation exclusion if > 20mmHg differential.

S. aureus (including MRSA in high-risk groups) is the causative organism in >75% of skin abscesses.
Incision and drainage (I&D) is the definitive treatment — antibiotics alone are not sufficient for a formed abscess.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)
• Attempt manual reduction: Trendelenburg + analgesia. Do NOT forcibly reduce if tender — strangulation risk.
• Emergency Theatre: irreducible / strangulated hernia — bowel resection risk, consent accordingly.
• Consent: hernia repair — recurrence (1–2% TAPP), chronic groin pain (5%), mesh infection (< 1%), testicular ischaemia/vas injury (< 1%), haematoma.

EMERGENCY LAPAROSCOPIC INGUINAL HERNIA REPAIR (TAPP) — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM from midnight. Consent signed.
• Antibiotics: Co-amoxiclav 1.2g IV at induction (optional — low infection risk if no mesh contamination).
• LMWH + TED stockings.
• Urinary catheter for bilateral or complex repairs (optional for unila …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.

• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.

PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.

• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 and D-dimer positive — exclude pulmonary embolism.

management.text: • Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Meropenem 1g TDS + Vancomycin 25mg/kg (septic shock — broad cover).
• IV fluid resuscitation: 30ml/kg Hartmann's bolus — reassess lactate and BP at 30 min.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Vasopressors: Noradrenaline 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min if MAP < 65 after 30ml/kg fluid.
• HDU/ICU admission — continuous BP monitoring, lactate trend.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Alvarado score: migration of pain (1), anorexia (1), nausea (1), RIF tenderness (2), rebound (1), elevated temp > 37.3 (1), leucocytosis (2), left shift (1). Score ≥ 7 = highly likely appendicitis.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg — antibiotic prophylaxis at induction.
β-HCG if female of reproductive age

LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)
• NG tube (16Fr): free drainage + 4-hourly aspiration. Document aspirate volume and character.
• IV Hartmann's 1–2L + IDC — fluid balance, electrolyte replacement (check K⁺ daily).
• CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast — level (SBO/LBO), transition point, closed loop, ischaemia (pneumatosis).
• If LBO due to colonic malignancy: colonic stent as bridge to elective resection (vs emergency Hartmann's).

BOWEL OBSTRUCTION — OPERATIVE PLAN (if conservative fails or signs of ischaemia)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY:
• Signs of bowel ischaemia (peritonism, lactate rising, pneumatosis on CT)
• Closed-loop obstruction on CT
• Complete SBO failing conservative management > 48h
• Strangulating hernia as cause

PRE-O …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Urine protein:creatinine ratio — nephrotic syndrome (PCR > 300mg/mmol).
• Dietitian referral — pre-operative nutritional support. Delay elective surgery ≥ 4 weeks if possible.
• Prescribe ONS (Ensure/Fortisip) ×2 — pre-op nutritional optimisation (ERAS).
• If albumin < 25 g/L and surgery urgent: parenteral nutrition pre-operatively with nutrition team support.
• Document last mammogram date — refer to radiology if overdue.
• Arrange bilateral mammogram — screening protocol.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.
• DXA bone density scan — osteoporosis screening (female ≥ 65).
• Vitamin D 800IU + Calcium 1200mg daily if deficient (osteoporosis prevention).

expectations.note: USPSTF 2021 / ACG 2021: average-risk screening from 45. ACG 2021: one FDR with CRC diagnosed < 60 (father at 58) → colonoscopy from age 40 (or 10 years before the relative’s age at diagnosis), repeated every 5 years — so he is overdue on the ACG reading. BSG 2020 (UK) would not add colonoscopic surveillance for a single FDR diagnosed ≥ 50. The practice’s policy needs the surgeon’s decision. Not observable in the web harness: the dashboard feeds the Family History field (ClinicalPromptsStrip familyHistory) to computeClinicalPrompts, but the vignette schema has no family-history input, so web-runner passes []. In the dashboard the "FHx colorectal cancer, age 35–49" prompt would probably add a colonoscopy. Needs a familyHistory input in the schema and both runners. Without a family history there is no screening prompt before 50: the average-risk "colorectal_screen" prompt starts at age 50 (USPSTF 2021 and ACG 2021: 45) and offers FOBT every 2 years rather than annual FIT.

management.text: • Ketones urgently — blood ketones > 3 mmol/L = DKA; urine ketones > 2+ = DKA screen positive.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII): DKA fixed-rate 0.1 units/kg/h. Monitor K⁺ hourly.
• Defer elective surgery — target glucose 6–10 mmol/L, ketones < 0.5 mmol/L pre-operatively.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Urine ketones — exclude diabetic ketoacidosis.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII) if inpatient glucose consistently > 11 mmol/L.
• Diabetology review — adjust long-term insulin/OHG regimen.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• Document last mammogram date — refer to radiology if overdue.
• Arrange bilateral mammogram — screening protocol.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.
• DXA bone density scan — osteoporosis screening (female ≥ 65).
• Vitamin D 800IU + Calcium 1200mg daily if deficient (osteoporosis prevention).

─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)

• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.

• Erect CXR — free air under diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum).
• 2 large-bore IV cannulae, Hartmann's 1L bolus, urinary catheter + fluid balance.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS + Metronidazole 500mg TDS.
• CT abdomen/pelvis — source of perforation, free fluid volume, staging.
• Emergency laparotomy consent — source control; ICU post-operatively.
• IV access, Hartmann's resuscitation, urinary catheter (fluid balance), NG tube (decompression).
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS + Metronidazole 500mg TDS.
• Emergency laparotomy consent — source control; ICU post-operatively.
• Do NOT delay theatre for further imaging — clinical + CXR diagnosis sufficient.
• 2 × large-bore IV cannulae, O-neg blood if haemodynamically unstable, cross-match 4 units.
• Emergency gynaecology referral — ruptured ectopic protocol, laparoscopic salpingectomy.
• Transvaginal USS if haemodynamically stable — confirm ectopic location before theatre.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Meropenem 1g TDS + Vancomycin 25mg/kg (septic shock — broad cover).
• IV fluid resuscitation: 30ml/kg Hartmann's bolus — reassess lactate and BP at 30 min.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Vasopressors: Noradrenaline 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min if MAP < 65 after 30ml/kg fluid.
• HDU/ICU admission — continuous BP monitoring, lactate trend.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Supplemental O₂: Hudson mask 5–10L/min, titrate to SpO₂ ≥ 94%.
• CXR — identify cause: consolidation, pneumothorax, effusion, cardiomegaly.
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 and D-dimer positive — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• Ketones urgently — blood ketones > 3 mmol/L = DKA; urine ketones > 2+ = DKA screen positive.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII): DKA fixed-rate 0.1 units/kg/h. Monitor K⁺ hourly.
• Defer elective surgery — target glucose 6–10 mmol/L, ketones < 0.5 mmol/L pre-operatively.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• Document last mammogram date — refer to radiology if overdue.
• Arrange bilateral mammogram — screening protocol.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.
• DXA bone density scan — osteoporosis screening (female ≥ 65).
• Vitamin D 800IU + Calcium 1200mg daily if deficient (osteoporosis prevention).

management.text: • Clinical diagnosis: do NOT delay exploration for imaging if torsion likely.
• Doppler USS scrotum — absent flow confirms torsion (use only if diagnosis uncertain).
• Emergency scrotal exploration — de-torsion, assess viability, bilateral fixation (orchidopexy).
• Surgical consent includes risk of orchidectomy (non-viable testis).
• Ketones urgently — blood ketones > 3 mmol/L = DKA; urine ketones > 2+ = DKA screen positive.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII): DKA fixed-rate 0.1 units/kg/h. Monitor K⁺ hourly.
• Defer elective surgery — target glucose 6–10 mmol/L, ketones < 0.5 mmol/L pre-operatively.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Urine ketones — exclude diabetic ketoacidosis.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII) if inpatient glucose consistently > 11 mmol/L.
• Diabetology review — adjust long-term insulin/OHG regimen.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• PSA discussion — document informed consent to proceed with test.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.

management.text: EMERGENCY — Strangulated Hernia
Emergency laparoscopic/open hernia repair. Assess bowel viability — resect if necrotic (primary anastomosis vs stoma based on contamination).
Do NOT delay for imaging if clinical peritonism is present.
[surgical] Elective: Lichtenstein mesh herniorrhaphy (local or GA) or laparoscopic TEP/TAPP.
[surgical] Emergency strangulated hernia: resuscitate, IV antibiotics, prompt surgery; bowel resection if non-viable.
Investigation: Clinical diagnosis (sufficient for uncomplicated hernia) (routine)
Investigation: FBC, U&E (pre-operative bloods) (urgent)
Investigation: USS (if diagnosis unclear or occult hernia) (routine)
Referral: General surgery — elective or emergency depending on presentation.
[surgical] Elective: Lichtenstein mesh herniorrhaphy (local or GA) or laparoscopic TEP/TAPP.
[surgical] Emergency strangulated hernia: resuscitate, IV antibiotics, prompt surgery; bowel resection if non-viable.
[conservative] Truss may be offered for unfit patients declining surgery — monitor for strangulation.
[followup] Review wound at 2 weeks; counsel on recurrence risk and mesh awareness.
Indirect inguinal hernia is the commonest hernia type (M:F ≈ 8:1 for inguinal; femoral M:F = 1:4).
Femoral hernias have higher strangulation risk — elective repair recommended regardless of symptoms.
Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is gold standard; laparoscopic (TEP/TAPP) equivalent outcomes.
• Erect CXR — free air under diaphragm (pneumoperitoneum).
• 2 large-bore IV cannulae, Hartmann's 1L bolus, urinary catheter + fluid balance.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS + Metronidazole 500mg TDS.
• CT abdomen/pelvis — source of perforation, free fluid volume, staging.
• Emergency laparotomy consent — source control; ICU post-operatively.
• Attempt manual reduction: Trendelenburg + analgesia. Do NOT forcibly reduce if tender — strangulation risk.
• Emergency Theatre: irreducible / strangulated hernia — bowel resection risk, consent accordingly.
• Consent: hernia repair — recurrence (1–2% TAPP), chronic groin pain (5%), mesh infection (< 1%), testicular ischaemia/vas injury (< 1%), haematoma.

management.text: Large Bowel Obstruction — Malignant
CT staging. Colorectal/Oncology MDT referral.
Options: (1) SEMS bridge to elective resection, (2) Emergency Hartmann's, (3) Defunctioning colostomy.
Decision based on: perforation risk, patient fitness, tumour stage, institutional expertise.
[surgical] Colon cancer: laparoscopic or open hemicolectomy / sigmoid colectomy with D3 lymphadenectomy.
[surgical] Rectal cancer: anterior resection (or APR for low tumours); TEMS / TEM for T1 disease.
[followup] Surveillance colonoscopy at 1 year, then 3-yearly; CEA + CT at 6-monthly intervals × 3 years.

Investigation: MRI pelvis (rectal cancer — CRM and T-stage) (urgent)
Referral: Colorectal MDT — urgent 2-week wait referral.
[surgical] Colon cancer: laparoscopic or open hemicolectomy / sigmoid colectomy with D3 lymphadenectomy.
[surgical] Rectal cancer: anterior resection (or APR for low tumours); TEMS / TEM for T1 disease.
[conservative] Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for T3/T4 or N+ rectal cancers before surgery.

• Alvarado score: migration of pain (1), anorexia (1), nausea (1), RIF tenderness (2), rebound (1), elevated temp > 37.3 (1), leucocytosis (2), left shift (1). Score ≥ 7 = highly likely appendicitis.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg — antibiotic prophylaxis at induction.
β-HCG if female of reproductive age

LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM — emergency case, starved status documented.
• IV Pip-Tazo 4.5g + Metronidazole 500mg at induction.
• LMWH + TED stockings (DVT prophylaxis).
• Consent obtained (emergency consent if incapacitated): perforation risk, conversion to open, wound infection, right-sided port-sit …(truncated)
• NG tube (16Fr): free drainage + 4-hourly aspiration. Document aspirate volume and character.
• IV Hartmann's 1–2L + IDC — fluid balance, electrolyte replacement (check K⁺ daily).
• CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast — level (SBO/LBO), transition point, closed loop, ischaemia (pneumatosis).
• If LBO due to colonic malignancy: colonic stent as bridge to elective resection (vs emergency Hartmann's).

BOWEL OBSTRUCTION — OPERATIVE PLAN (if conservative fails or signs of ischaemia)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY:
• Signs of bowel ischaemia (peritonism, lactate rising, pneumatosis on CT)
• Closed-loop obstruction on CT
• Complete SBO failing conservative management > 48h
• Strangulating hernia as cause

PRE-O …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g TDS — empirical sepsis cover.
• IV Hartmann's 1L over 4h — ensure adequate hydration.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.
• Document bilateral BP — coarctation exclusion if > 20mmHg differential.
• Document last mammogram date — refer to radiology if overdue.
• Arrange bilateral mammogram — screening protocol.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.
• DXA bone density scan — osteoporosis screening (female ≥ 65).
• Vitamin D 800IU + Calcium 1200mg daily if deficient (osteoporosis prevention).

Life-threatening surgical emergency — mortality 25–35%; every hour's delay worsens outcome.
Type I (polymicrobial — Meleney's, Fournier's) and Type II (Group A Streptococcus) are the two main types.
LRINEC score >6 raises suspicion; do NOT wait for CT or laboratory confirmation if the diagnosis is clinically likely.
• Clinical diagnosis: do NOT delay exploration for imaging if torsion likely.
• Doppler USS scrotum — absent flow confirms torsion (use only if diagnosis uncertain).
• Emergency scrotal exploration — de-torsion, assess viability, bilateral fixation (orchidopexy).
• Surgical consent includes risk of orchidectomy (non-viable testis).
• Blood cultures × 2 before antibiotics.
• IV Meropenem 1g TDS + Vancomycin 25mg/kg (septic shock — broad cover).
• IV fluid resuscitation: 30ml/kg Hartmann's bolus — reassess lactate and BP at 30 min.
• Urinary catheter — strict fluid balance, urine output ≥ 0.5ml/kg/h.
• Vasopressors: Noradrenaline 0.01–0.5 mcg/kg/min if MAP < 65 after 30ml/kg fluid.
• HDU/ICU admission — continuous BP monitoring, lactate trend.
• Identify source of infection: CXR + urine dipstick + abdominal CT if no clear focus.
• Ketones urgently — blood ketones > 3 mmol/L = DKA; urine ketones > 2+ = DKA screen positive.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII): DKA fixed-rate 0.1 units/kg/h. Monitor K⁺ hourly.
• Defer elective surgery — target glucose 6–10 mmol/L, ketones < 0.5 mmol/L pre-operatively.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• Urine Na (> 20: SIADH/renal loss; < 20: hypovolaemic/oedematous states), urine osmolality, serum osmolality.
• Review medications for SIADH causes: diuretics, SSRIs, carbamazepine.
• Exclude secondary SIADH causes: CXR (lung malignancy), CT head (CNS lesion/meningitis).
• Fluid restriction 1L/day — euvolaemic SIADH. Correct slowly.
• Elective surgery deferred — sodium < 130 mmol/L anaesthetic risk; target ≥ 130 pre-op.
• Urine ketones — exclude diabetic ketoacidosis.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII) if inpatient glucose consistently > 11 mmol/L.
• Diabetology review — adjust long-term insulin/OHG regimen.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.
• Document bilateral BP — coarctation exclusion if > 20mmHg differential.
• PSA discussion — document informed consent to proceed with test.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.

• If urine β-HCG positive: serum quantitative β-HCG + urgent TVS — exclude ectopic.
• If ectopic suspected: emergency gynaecology referral — surgical or medical management.
• Ketones urgently — blood ketones > 3 mmol/L = DKA; urine ketones > 2+ = DKA screen positive.

• Alvarado score: migration of pain (1), anorexia (1), nausea (1), RIF tenderness (2), rebound (1), elevated temp > 37.3 (1), leucocytosis (2), left shift (1). Score ≥ 7 = highly likely appendicitis.

• Refer diabetology — insulin regimen intensification or OHG escalation.
• Delay elective surgery 4–8 weeks — target HbA1c < 8.5% / 69 mmol/mol pre-operatively.
• If HbA1c > 10%: pre-operative VRIII on day of surgery — glucose target 6–10 mmol/L intraoperatively.
• Diabetic foot exam + urine ACR — complication screen before anaesthetic.
• Urine ketones — exclude diabetic ketoacidosis.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII) if inpatient glucose consistently > 11 mmol/L.
• Diabetology review — adjust long-term insulin/OHG regimen.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• Confirm cervical smear date — document last result.
• Refer gynaecology — cervical smear overdue (> 3 years).

management.text: [immediate] Ruptured AAA: two large-bore IV cannulae, cross-match 6 units RBC, permissive hypotension (systolic 70–80 mmHg) until in theatre.
[conservative] Small AAA (3.0–5.4 cm): surveillance ultrasound 3-yearly (3–4.4 cm) or annually (4.5–5.4 cm).
[conservative] Cardiovascular risk reduction: statin, antiplatelet, smoking cessation, blood pressure control.
[surgical] Elective repair for AAA ≥5.5 cm (men) / ≥5.0 cm (women), or symptomatic/rapidly expanding: EVAR preferred where anatomy permits.
[surgical] Open surgical repair (midline laparotomy, aortic graft) for anatomy unsuitable for EVAR or EVAR failure.
[followup] Post-EVAR: CT at 1 month, 12 months, then annually for endoleak surveillance.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA): defined as aortic diameter >3 cm; risk of rupture rises sharply above 5.5 cm (men) and 5.0 cm (women).
Rupture presents as triad of hypotension, back/abdominal pain, and pulsatile abdominal mass — mortality without surgery >90%.
Symptomatic or rapidly expanding AAA (>1 cm/year or >0.5 cm/6 months) warrants urgent repair regardless of size.
• 2 × large-bore IV cannulae, Hartmann's 1L bolus — reassess BP and HR at 15 min.
• 12-lead ECG — ST elevation MI, arrhythmia, right heart strain (PE).
• Portable CXR — cardiac outline, pulmonary oedema, pneumothorax.
• POCUS: cardiac (effusion/tamponade), aorta (AAA), IVC collapsibility.
• Contact appropriate specialty immediately: cardiology (MI/tamponade), surgery (haemorrhage/AAA), emergency medicine (PE).
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• 12-lead ECG — arrhythmia, right heart strain pattern (PE).
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• IV fluid challenge 500ml if hypovolaemia likely — reassess HR at 30 min.
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.

management.text: Severe Acute Pancreatitis — ICU Level Care
ICU admission. Aggressive resuscitation. Enteral feeding via NGT/NJT within 24–48 h (superior to TPN).
Carbapenem antibiotics (meropenem) ONLY if infected necrosis suspected (fever + gas in necrotic area on CT).
Necrosectomy: step-up approach (endoscopic > percutaneous > surgical) — delayed ≥4 weeks until walled-off.
[immediate] Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Hartmann's 250–500 ml/h initial).
[immediate] Analgesia: IV morphine or pethidine; antiemetics.
[immediate] NBM — enteral feeding via NG/NJ if not tolerating PO at 48 h.
[surgical] Infected necrosis (CECT confirmed): step-up approach — percutaneous drain → video-assisted retroperitoneal debridement (VARD).
[followup] Interval cholecystectomy for gallstone aetiology if not done in-patient.
[followup] Pancreatic function testing (exocrine / endocrine) after severe episode.

CT with IV contrast (CECT) at 48–72 h if no improvement — assess for necrosis.
• NG tube (16Fr): free drainage + 4-hourly aspiration. Document aspirate volume and character.
• IV Hartmann's 1–2L + IDC — fluid balance, electrolyte replacement (check K⁺ daily).
• CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast — level (SBO/LBO), transition point, closed loop, ischaemia (pneumatosis).
• If LBO due to colonic malignancy: colonic stent as bridge to elective resection (vs emergency Hartmann's).

BOWEL OBSTRUCTION — OPERATIVE PLAN (if conservative fails or signs of ischaemia)
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY:
• Signs of bowel ischaemia (peritonism, lactate rising, pneumatosis on CT)
• Closed-loop obstruction on CT
• Complete SBO failing conservative management > 48h
• Strangulating hernia as cause

PRE-O …(truncated)
• Erect CXR — exclude free air and basal pneumonia.
• 12-lead ECG — pre-operative cardiac baseline (age ≥ 40).
• Blood cultures × 2 before first antibiotic dose.
• Sepsis-6 bundle: O₂, cultures, antibiotics, IV fluids, urine output monitoring, blood glucose.
• CT abdomen if abdominal source suspected — abscess, perforation, ischaemia.
• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• MRCP — CBD diameter, stone burden, biliary stricture characterisation.
• ERCP — therapeutic: stone extraction (choledocholithiasis) or stenting (malignant stricture).
• HPB surgical review — Whipple / Hartmann's if resectable malignancy.
• Supplemental O₂: Hudson mask 5–10L/min, titrate to SpO₂ ≥ 94%.
• CXR — identify cause: consolidation, pneumothorax, effusion, cardiomegaly.
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 and D-dimer positive — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• 12-lead ECG — arrhythmia, right heart strain pattern (PE).
• CTPA if Wells score ≥ 2 — exclude pulmonary embolism.
• IV fluid challenge 500ml if hypovolaemia likely — reassess HR at 30 min.
• Urine protein:creatinine ratio — nephrotic syndrome (PCR > 300mg/mmol).
• Dietitian referral — pre-operative nutritional support. Delay elective surgery ≥ 4 weeks if possible.
• Prescribe ONS (Ensure/Fortisip) ×2 — pre-op nutritional optimisation (ERAS).
• If albumin < 25 g/L and surgery urgent: parenteral nutrition pre-operatively with nutrition team support.
• USS RUQ — gallbladder wall thickness (> 4mm), pericholecystic fluid, stones, CBD diameter.
• Consent: laparoscopic cholecystectomy — bile duct injury (0.3%), haemorrhage, conversion to open, bile leak, retained stone, wound infection.

LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY — OPERATIVE PLAN
─────────────────────────────────────────────
PRE-OPERATIVE:
• NBM from midnight (or ≥ 6h solids / 2h clear fluids).
• IV Co-amoxiclav 1.2g at induction (single prophylactic dose).
• LMWH (Enoxaparin 40mg SC) night before + day of surgery; TED stockings.
• IV access; identify allergy status.
• Consent signed and documented.

ANAESTHESIA:  …(truncated)
• Urine ketones — exclude diabetic ketoacidosis.
• Variable-rate insulin infusion (VRIII) if inpatient glucose consistently > 11 mmol/L.
• Diabetology review — adjust long-term insulin/OHG regimen.
• Urine albumin:creatinine ratio — diabetic nephropathy screening.
• PSA discussion — document informed consent to proceed with test.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.

expectations.detail: forbidden management item present in web.plan: "icu admission. aggressive resuscitation. enteral feeding via ngt/njt within 24-48 h (superior to tpn)." (+3 more) [known gap: Plan tab: "Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (Hartmann's 250–500 ml/h)" in established respiratory failure with pleural effusions.]
expectations.note: WATERFALL (NEJM 2022) was stopped for harm: aggressive resuscitation (20 mL/kg bolus then 3 mL/kg/h) caused more fluid overload (20.5% vs 6.3%) without benefit. ACG 2024 recommends moderate, goal-directed fluids. A plan that says "aggressive" or 250–500 mL/h is a fluid-overload hazard. In established organ failure with respiratory failure and pleural effusions, fluid overload worsens outcome.
expectations.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine management protocol "pancreatitis" (step 1 and the Hartmann's 500 ml Q2H medication), dx-variants.ts pancreatitis_moderate urgencyNote / pancreatitis_severe planPrefix, and clinical-inference.ts pancreatitis prompts: replace "aggressive … 250–500 ml/h" with moderate goal-directed lactated Ringer's (10 mL/kg bolus only if hypovolaemic, then 1.5 mL/kg/h; reassess at 12, 24, 48, 72 h; extra caution in heart failure/CKD/elderly) citing WATERFALL and ACG 2024. Same change in iOS DiagnosisRadiationEngine "acute pancreatitis" planTemplate.

CBD stones cause 10–15% of all biliary colic presentations; risk rises with gallbladder stones.
MRCP is gold standard non-invasive imaging (>95% sensitivity); USS CBD dilation suggests obstruction.
ERCP is both diagnostic and therapeutic — sphincterotomy clears stones in 90%.

• Urine dipstick, urinalysis, albumin:creatinine ratio — AKI vs CKD differentiation.
• Hold NSAIDs, ACE-I, ARBs, metformin — nephrotoxic drugs peri-operatively.
• IV fluid challenge (500ml Hartmann's) if pre-renal cause — reassess creatinine in 4–6h.
• Consider nephrology input if creatinine not improving after fluid resuscitation.
• 12-lead ECG urgently — peaked T-waves, widened QRS, AV block, sine wave pattern.
• IV Actrapid 10 units + 50ml 50% dextrose — shift K⁺ intracellularly. Onset 15–30 min, duration 6h. Monitor BGL.
• Nebulised salbutamol 10–20mg — adjunct K⁺ shift (additive to insulin-dextrose).
• Identify and treat cause: hold ACE-I/ARBs/spironolactone; assess for AKI, rhabdomyolysis.
• Surgery DEFERRED — K⁺ must be < 5.5 mmol/L before any general or regional anaesthesia.
• Urine ACR — hypertensive nephropathy screen.
• Document bilateral BP — coarctation exclusion if > 20mmHg differential.
• Hold NSAIDs 48h pre-operatively — renal protection.
• PSA discussion — document informed consent to proceed with test.
• Faecal occult blood test — CRC screening (if colonoscopy declined).
• Colonoscopy — CRC screening, age ≥ 50.

management.text: [immediate] Ruptured AAA: two large-bore IV cannulae, cross-match 6 units RBC, permissive hypotension (systolic 70–80 mmHg) until in theatre.
[conservative] Small AAA (3.0–5.4 cm): surveillance ultrasound 3-yearly (3–4.4 cm) or annually (4.5–5.4 cm).
[conservative] Cardiovascular risk reduction: statin, antiplatelet, smoking cessation, blood pressure control.
[surgical] Elective repair for AAA ≥5.5 cm (men) / ≥5.0 cm (women), or symptomatic/rapidly expanding: EVAR preferred where anatomy permits.
[surgical] Open surgical repair (midline laparotomy, aortic graft) for anatomy unsuitable for EVAR or EVAR failure.
[followup] Post-EVAR: CT at 1 month, 12 months, then annually for endoleak surveillance.
Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA): defined as aortic diameter >3 cm; risk of rupture rises sharply above 5.5 cm (men) and 5.0 cm (women).
Rupture presents as triad of hypotension, back/abdominal pain, and pulsatile abdominal mass — mortality without surgery >90%.
Symptomatic or rapidly expanding AAA (>1 cm/year or >0.5 cm/6 months) warrants urgent repair regardless of size.

management.text: Small Bowel Obstruction — Non-Operative Trial (Drip and Suck)
NGT on free drainage. IV fluid resuscitation. NBM. Serial clinical assessment every 4–6 h.
CT abdomen/pelvis to exclude closed-loop, ischaemia, or hernia.
Failure criteria at 48–72 h: no resolution, worsening pain, peritonism, fever, rising lactate → operate.
[immediate] IV access, IV fluids (correct dehydration and electrolytes), catheter.
[immediate] NG tube insertion — "drip and suck" decompression.
[immediate] Analgesia, antiemetics.
[conservative] Adhesive SBO: conservative 48 h trial if no peritonism; water-soluble contrast study at 24 h.
[followup] Elective laparoscopic adhesiolysis for recurrent adhesive obstruction.
Investigation: FBC, U&E, lactate (urgent)
Investigation: Group & save (urgent)
Investigation: AXR (dilated loops, air-fluid levels) (urgent)
Investigation: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast (level, cause, ischaemia) (urgent)
Referral: Emergency surgical admission.
[immediate] Drip and suck: NGT decompression, IV fluids, catheter (hourly UO), NBM; correct electrolytes.
[conservative] Gastrografin challenge at 24 h (100 mL oral / NGT) — if contrast reaches colon in 24 h, >95% resolve without surgery.
[surgical] Failure to resolve at 48–72 h, or ischaemia signs — emergency laparoscopy or laparotomy + adhesiolysis.
[surgical] Ischaemic bowel: resection ± primary anastomosis (Hartmann's if contaminated).
[followup] Counsel on recurrence risk (30% at 10 years); consider Seprafilm / icodextrin barrier at index surgery.
Adhesions account for 60% of all SBO — risk peaks within 5 years of laparotomy but continues lifelong.
Gastrografin (water-soluble contrast) challenge at 24 h both predicts and promotes resolution without surgery (65–80% success).
Closed-loop obstruction or ischaemic signs (constant pain, pyrexia, raised lactate) demand emergency surgery.
• Attempt manual reduction: Trendelenburg + analgesia. Do NOT forcibly reduce if tender — strangulation risk.

• Consent: hernia repair — recurrence (1–2% TAPP), chronic groin pain (5%), mesh infection (< 1%), testicular ischaemia/vas injury (< 1%), haematoma.

• LMWH + TED stockings.
• Urinary catheter for bilateral or complex repairs (optional for unila …(truncated)

management.text: Total Thyroidectomy
Total thyroidectomy ± central compartment neck dissection (level VI) for confirmed malignancy.
Intraoperative RLN monitoring. Post-op: levothyroxine replacement (lifelong). Monitor calcium × 24 h — oral calcium if symptomatic hypocalcaemia.
[surgical] Large / expanding haematoma: return to theatre — evacuate clot, achieve haemostasis, re-close or VAC.
[surgical] Cervical haematoma with airway compromise: immediate wound opening at bedside (undo sutures + skin clips), secure airway, emergency re-operation.
[followup] Review anticoagulation plan with haematology / cardiology post-event; wound review at 2 weeks.
Investigation: Clinical examination (tense, swollen wound, bruising) (routine)
Investigation: FBC, coagulation screen (identify coagulopathy) (urgent)
Investigation: USS wound (confirm haematoma, guide aspiration of liquefied collections) (routine)
Referral: Surgical emergency (expanding / neck haematoma); elective surgical clinic for stable cases.
Protamine sulfate 1 mg per 100 units heparin given in last 4 h IV (intravenous) slow injection Single dose over 10 min — Heparin reversal — calculate dose based on heparin given in last 4 h
Vitamin K (phytomenadione) 10 mg IV (intravenous) slow injection Single dose (onset 6 h) — Warfarin reversal
Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) 15 mL/kg IV (intravenous) infusion Single infusion — repeat if INR not corrected — Warfarin reversal bridge while vitamin K takes effect
Idarucizumab (Praxbind) 5 g IV (intravenous) Two doses of 2.5 g IV over 5–10 min each — Dabigatran reversal
Andexanet alfa (Ondexxya) Per weight/dose protocol — IV bolus then infusion IV (intravenous) Single treatment course — Rivaroxaban / apixaban reversal — if available
Tranexamic acid 1 g IV (intravenous) Single dose (can repeat at 8 h if ongoing haemorrhage) — Haemostasis promotion for expanding haematoma
Paracetamol 1 g PO / IV (oral or intravenous) QDS (four times daily) — Analgesia — avoid NSAIDs (antiplatelet effect)
[conservative] Small haematoma (<5 cm): elevate, pressure dressing; review coagulation; withhold anticoagulants; observe 24 h.
[surgical] Large / expanding haematoma: return to theatre — evacuate clot, achieve haemostasis, re-close or VAC.
[surgical] Cervical haematoma with airway compromise: immediate wound opening at bedside (undo sutures + skin clips), secure airway, emergency re-operation.
[conservative] Reverse anticoagulation if safe (protamine for heparin; vitamin K + FFP for warfarin; idarucizumab for dabigatran).
[followup] Review anticoagulation plan with haematology / cardiology post-event; wound review at 2 weeks.
Post-operative haematoma occurs in 1–3% of wounds — risk increased by anticoagulation, antiplatelet therapy, hypertension, and poor haemostasis.
Expanding haematoma in the neck (post-thyroid / carotid) can compress the airway — a true surgical emergency.
Most small haematomas are absorbed; large or expanding require surgical evacuation.

• CXR — identify cause: consolidation, pneumothorax, effusion, cardiomegaly.

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY:
• Signs of bowel ischaemia (peritonism, lactate rising, pneumatosis on CT)
• Closed-loop obstruction on CT
• Complete SBO failing conservative management > 48h
• Strangulating hernia as cause
